_disclaimer: SIMULATED DEMONSTRATION CONFIGURATION. These are escalation triggers for a prototype. They are not a validated screening instrument, they have not been tested against real presentations, and the system does not claim to detect cardiac arrest, stroke or any other condition. It identifies phrases and observations that MAY indicate a life-threatening situation and escalates them for human attention.
_design: Two independent layers. The RULE layer fires on the patient's own words and on objective observations, always, with no network and no model. The MODEL layer may add triggers the rules missed. The model can only ADD: it has no path to clear a rule trigger, so a model failure degrades detection to the rule floor rather than removing it. This is the same asymmetry as the Ratchet, applied to the emergency gate.
_sensitivity: Deliberately over-sensitive. A false emergency costs a nurse thirty seconds of attention. A missed one is the failure this whole project exists to reduce. Every trigger is recorded with the exact phrase and timestamp so a nurse can dismiss it in one click and so the false-positive rate is measurable rather than assumed.

settings.patient_message: We are getting someone to you now. Please stay where you are.
settings._patient_message_note: What the patient sees. Deliberately not 'EMERGENCY DETECTED' in red: telling a frightened person that a computer thinks they are dying is not care, and panic makes assessment harder. The nurse screen is where the alarm belongs.
